subject.title: [Feature]: Compaction: configurable model override + flush-then-reset mode

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in normal success-path mode that resets a session immediately after a successful agentic memory flush instead of running compaction, and what config, consent, timeout, audit, and security boundaries should govern it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing this behavior changes silent model execution, provider routing, session-state retention, and privacy/security semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent policy.

options.title: Design bounded reset-after-flush
options.body: Approve an explicit opt-in lifecycle mode with timeout, duplicate-reset protection, durable-memory expectations, user or audit visibility, and security constraints before implementation.

options.title: Fold into reset-memory policy
options.body: Track the remaining behavior under the open reset-memory issue so reset-time and compaction-time session rotation share one lifecycle contract.

options.title: Keep compaction as the supported path
options.body: Decline automatic reset-after-flush and keep current model overrides plus compaction/exhaustion recovery as the supported maintenance behavior.

recommendation.title: Design bounded reset-after-flush
recommendation.body: Approve an explicit opt-in lifecycle mode with timeout, duplicate-reset protection, durable-memory expectations, user or audit visibility, and security constraints before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to both pre-compaction memory flush and reset handling, which makes them the best available owner for the cross-boundary product decision.
